Large estates growing the African oil palm for its oil, which began in Malaya in 1917. Today Malaysia and Indonesia produce most of the world's palm oil.

The oil palm is native to West Africa. A few seedlings reached the botanic garden at Bogor in the Dutch East Indies in 1848, and planters in Sumatra and then Malaya found it grew better there than at home. The first commercial estate in Malaya opened in Selangor in 1917, alongside the rubber that then ruled the colony's plantations.

After independence, Malaysia moved poor rural families onto new land under the Federal Land Development Authority, and much of it went to oil palm. Indonesia expanded even faster from the 1980s. Palm oil is cheap and versatile and ends up in cooking oil, margarine, soap, biscuits and biofuel.

The cost has fallen on the rainforest. Clearing for plantations destroyed habitat for the orangutan and other animals, and fires on drained peat send smoke haze across the region in dry years.
sum: Large estates growing the African oil palm for its oil, which began in Malaya in 1917. Today Malaysia and Indonesia produce most of the world's palm oil.
